title: Wanting to play trumpet but being steered to clarinet
summary: He wanted trumpet but his family said he lacked wind and, since he whistled well, urged clarinet; he later felt too far gone on clarinet to switch.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Romansky, I was about 13, 14 years old. Then I began to study hard and liking music. But first I wanted to be a trumpet player.
Did you ever play the trumpet?

No. I tried it. I was coming along good, but only after I got big, you know, because my folks says, "Son, you don't have enough wind to blow the trumpet." And I could whistle good, so they decided to say, "Why don't you take up the clarinet?" And I said, "Well." They said, "Because you whistle good." And I said, "Well, I'll try it."
But I didn't care for the clarinet that much. I liked the trumpet better. But they didn't want me to take up trumpet. So I took clarinet, and that's what it was, clarinet.
Well, later when you tried playing the trumpet, did you think you would like it or not?

Well, I was too far gone on the clarinet then, you know, and I didn't want to start that trumpet all over again, so I -- if I did, I would just be just to play it a player like, probably like Benny Carter would, you know, [crossed out]. I wouldn't want to stay with it, I don't think. But otherwise, all right.
